inspiration_source: Mammalian long bone / femoral neck: dense cortical shell around stress-aligned cancellous (trabecular) bone, cross-mapped to aerospace sandwich panels and Wolff's law of functional adaptation
physical_mechanism: Bone places dense cortical material far from the neutral axis, where bending stresses are largest, and fills the interior with a low-density trabecular lattice whose struts align with principal stress trajectories (Wolff's law). The lattice carries shear, stabilises the thin shell against local buckling and adds little mass. In the beam, a thin solid shell (thickness t) encloses an open-cell trabecular core of relative density rho*. The core's effective modulus follows the Gibson-Ashby scaling for bending-dominated foams, E_core = E_s * rho*^2, so the flexural rigidity is EI = E_s*I_shell + E_s*rho*^2*I_core. Almost all of the second moment of area comes from the shell, so mass drops a lot while stiffness drops only a little. For a simply supported beam of span L under uniform load q, the bending moment from statics is M(x) = q x (L - x)/2, and the deflection follows from EI w'' = -M(x) with w(0) = w(L) = 0. The maximum is w_max = 5 q L^4 / (384 EI).

parameters.name: span_length
parameters.justification: Span L [m] of a lightweight structural member, e.g. a frame or boom element; about 2-3x the length of a human femur, scaled up for engineering use.

parameters.name: uniform_load
parameters.justification: Distributed line load q [N/m], typical service load for a light structural beam.

parameters.name: solid_youngs_modulus
parameters.justification: Young's modulus E_s [Pa] of the parent material (additively manufactured Al alloy, 70 GPa). Bounds range from cortical-bone-like composites (~15-20 GPa) to Ti alloys (~110 GPa).

parameters.name: beam_height
parameters.justification: Outer cross-section height h [m]. Span/height of 10 is a typical ratio for slender beams, where Euler-Bernoulli theory is still valid.

parameters.name: cortical_thickness
parameters.justification: Shell (cortical) wall thickness t [m]. The bone cortex-to-diameter ratio is roughly 0.05-0.15; t/h = 0.04 is at the lightweight end.

parameters.name: trabecular_relative_density
parameters.justification: Relative density rho* of the trabecular core lattice. Human cancellous bone is 0.05-0.5, and printable lattices are typically 0.1-0.3. The core modulus scales as E_s*rho*^2 (Gibson-Ashby).
